transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello. Well... I suppose I'm just here because, for the past year or so, I... I feel like I'm always puttering around. Fixing things, arranging... volunteering for one more thing. 

I'm 87, so you'd think I'd rest, but... I just have a hard time sitting down and being still. That's really it.
Do you find yourself having repeated, unwanted thoughts that bother you, or do you feel the need to perform certain actions repeatedly to ease your anxiety?
No... I don't think so. I don't really have thoughts like that. And I'm not doing things because I'm anxious, I just... well, I just do them.
Do you ever have thoughts or impulses that come into your mind that you find upsetting or that you can't seem to get rid of, even if you try not to think about them?
No... I can't say that I do. Nothing like that.
Do you ever feel like you have to do certain things in a very specific way or at certain times, even if you don’t want to?
No... not really. I just do whatever needs doing. It doesn't have to be a certain way or anything.
Have you ever felt like your mind gets stuck on certain thoughts or ideas, even if you don't want to think about them, and it's hard to let them go?
No... I don't think so. Like I said, I don't really get stuck on things. I just... move on to the next thing, I suppose.
Do you often feel worried or anxious about things in your daily life, even when there's no clear reason for concern?
No... I wouldn't say so. If there's no reason to worry about something, I just... I don't worry about it.
Do you ever feel bothered by your tendency to keep busy, or has it ever caused problems for you or those around you?

Well... I suppose it has, sometimes. Just... at the senior center. I've had to apologize after some of our meetings. And... a friend of mine suggested I take a smaller role at the sign-up table. She said my manner was making things a bit tense. So... yes, I guess.
Even when there's nothing that needs to be done, do you find it hard to relax or feel restless?

I suppose... yes, sometimes. Like... if I'm at the senior center meetings, or... sitting through the long announcements at church. I just get this... well, an ants-in-my-chair sort of feeling. I usually have to shift around a bit, or... maybe stand up to get some coffee. Or I'll just straighten the papers in front of me. Just to... get through it, I suppose.
Would you say that this restlessness or need to stay busy has caused you noticeable distress or has interfered with your life in any important way?

Well... like I mentioned a moment ago, it's mostly just... the senior center. I wouldn't use a strong word like distress. But... having to apologize after those meetings, and... my friend telling me to step back from the sign-up table because I was making people tense... I suppose that's an interference. It's just... not ideal. That's all.
Do you find it hard to focus or stay attentive during conversations or tasks, even when there's nothing else going on around you?
Well... no, I don't think so. I can follow a conversation just fine. I haven't really noticed any trouble with that.
Do you ever find yourself acting on impulse without thinking things through, or do you have trouble waiting your turn in situations?

Well... I suppose waiting can be a bit bothersome. Like... if I'm in the sign-up line, or when they're handing out supplies. I get a bit fidgety. 

I might catch myself sighing, or... checking my watch. Sometimes I end up edging forward when I really should just stand there and wait my turn. I get a bit short, I guess. But... that's about it.
Do you ever find yourself easily distracted by things around you, even when you're trying to focus on something important?
No... not really. If I need to focus on something, I just do. I haven't noticed any... particular problems with being distracted.
Do you ever have trouble finishing tasks, or do you often lose track of what you're supposed to be doing, even if it's something simple?
No... I don't believe so. If I start something, I just finish it. I haven't really noticed myself losing track of what I'm doing.
Do other people ever comment on you fidgeting, moving around, or seeming restless when you're trying to sit still?

Well... I suppose sometimes. Not often, but... maybe at the senior center meetings. Or... during the long announcements at church. 

I just... I get this sort of ants-in-my-chair feeling, I guess. I might shift around a bit. Or I'll stand up to go get a coffee, or just... straighten some papers. Just to get through it, really. I don't think it's a big deal, but... people might have mentioned it once or twice.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing, even for just a few days?
No... I can't say that I have. I sleep my usual amount, really. I haven't noticed anything... unusual like that.
Do you often feel that things have to be done a certain way, and does it bother you when other people don't do things the way you think they should be done?
No... I wouldn't say so. I just... let people do things their way. It doesn't really bother me.
Do you ever find it difficult to stay focused on tasks or conversations, even when you're trying to pay attention?
No... I don't think so. I can pay attention just fine when I need to. I haven't really noticed any trouble with that.
Looking back, would you say that you were noticeably restless, had trouble focusing, or acted without thinking when you were younger—say, before you turned 12?

Well... I suppose so. That was a very long time ago. But... yes, I remember getting scolded in grade school. For popping out of my seat, mostly. And... talking over the other children. They used to tell my parents I was just 'too lively.' That was... well, long before I was a teenager.
Looking back, would you say that before you turned 12, you had a lot of trouble sitting still, staying focused, or acting without thinking?

I... well, I believe we just spoke about that. Like I said, yes, I had a hard time staying in my chair back then. But I don't really remember much else to tell you. It was nearly eighty years ago, after all.
